grammatical_complexity.notes: Dominated by past simple with dialogue in present/simple past. Past perfect and reported speech appear in the final paragraphs. Subordinate clauses are scattered throughout. Complex structures appear in roughly 20-25% of sentences.

cultural_reference_load.notes: Mostly globally recognizable references. Starbucks and Vancouver are well-known. 'Bucks' as slang and 'two cream' coffee ordering are mildly North American but inferable from context. No customs that would block comprehension.

sentence_structure.notes: Mix of very short dialogue lines and moderate narrative sentences. Mostly subject-verb-object with some compound sentences. A few longer sentences with subordinate clauses but nothing over 25 words.

items.context: get me a large coffee with two cream
items.reason: 'Large coffee' is a globally understood phrase due to international coffee chains. Context makes the size meaning unmistakable.

items.context: We can give you a test
items.reason: Spanish 'test' is borrowed from English and means exam/trial. The meaning here is essentially identical. No confusion likely.
